content: Perinatal Assistants are specialized professionals who provide comprehensive support throughout the childbearing year. Their services encompass a range of roles, including those of a doula, childbirth educator, postpartum support provider, and breastfeeding support specialist. The training required to become a Perinatal Assistant involves a rigorous program lasting a minimum of ten months. This program includes in-depth instruction in anatomy and physiology, the physiological processes of childbirth, labor support techniques, breastfeeding management, postpartum care, and educational and teaching methodologies. Additionally, the program requires the completion of a thesis and a final examination. This educational pathway typically leads to either a Diploma or an Associate Degree. At present, the only officially registered Perinatal Assistant education program is provided by the Global Birth Institute.
